q3.title: AI in use across the organization

q3.html:
Developer AI tools
Medium
Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor are in use across engineering. Exposure: code provenance, secrets leaking into prompts, and license/IP contamination.
Measured against OWASP LLM05 · LLM02 · SLSA
Agentic AI
High
Autonomous agents hold tool access to CI/CD, ticketing, and data stores. Exposure: over-broad permissions and unbounded actions — an agent acts faster than oversight.
Measured against OWASP Agentic AI · NIST AI RMF
Shadow AI
High
Unsanctioned LLM use, some touching PHI, outside DLP. Exposure: PHI sent to third-party models with no audit trail.
Measured against HIPAA · OWASP LLM06
AI in claims decisions
High
Models make claims decisions on PHI without human oversight. Exposure: bias, hallucination, and no documented defensibility.
Measured against EU AI Act (high-risk) · NIST AI RMF

q3.label: If an agentic AI tool with production access is compromised or misbehaves →
q3.html: It can act at machine speed across CI/CD, ticketing, and data stores — exfiltrating data or making changes faster than any human reviewer can intervene. Governing agent permissions and adopting the OWASP Agentic AI controls is the mitigation, and the basis for the AI-governance decision.

q4.lead: Treat the risk, hold owners accountable, and set the enterprise AI standard — each with the cost of every path.

items.title: Accept, transfer, or mitigate vendor (PHI) risk
items.sit: A critical vendor handling PHI is below tolerance. The classic risk-treatment choice — each option has a different cost and residual.

options.name: A · Mitigate (tighten controls)
options.outcome: Vendor access scoped down, monitoring added; brings the risk back within appetite.

options.name: B · Transfer (insurance / contract)
options.outcome: Shifts financial impact via coverage and indemnity; risk event still possible.
options.tradeoff: Recurring cost; event can still occur.

options.name: C · Accept with documentation
options.outcome: Formally accept the residual risk; no spend.
options.tradeoff: Above-appetite risk remains on the register.

items.rec: Recommendation: Option A (mitigate). At $240K it actually reduces likelihood and returns the risk within appetite, versus transfer which only caps the loss or acceptance which leaves you above the line.

items.title: Establish enterprise AI governance & standards
items.sit: Developer, agentic, and shadow AI are in use ahead of governance. As risk owner, you set the enterprise standard every other leader executes against.

options.name: A · Adopt NIST AI RMF + OWASP, govern agents
options.outcome: Enterprise AI standard, model inventory, agent-permission governance, monitoring.
options.risk: Brings AI risk within appetite · EU AI Act ready

options.name: B · Interim guardrails only
options.outcome: Block shadow AI, scope agent permissions, sanction approved tools.
options.tradeoff: No standards program; revisit next cycle.

items.rec: Recommendation: Option A. AI risk is compounding; an enterprise standard with agent-permission governance is what holds each leader accountable and gets you EU AI Act–ready before the claims model is classified high-risk.
